# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 72 (Bi-Vb Pc72)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 72. Ordaining an untrained unmarried woman
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining an untrained unmarried woman

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

**Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 72** (titled *Paripuṇṇavīsativassa-asikkhita-kumāribhūta*) governs the conditions for ordaining an unmarried woman (*kumārībhūtā*) [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009; Hüsken 1997]. The rule stipulates that a nun commits an expiation offense (*pācittiya*) if she confers full ordination (*vuṭṭhāpeyya*) upon an unmarried woman who has attained the age of twenty but has not completed the required two years of training in the six rules as a probationer (*sikkhamānā*) [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009; Hüsken 1997]. 

Modern scholarship notes that the canonical text permits granting the two-year training agreement to an unmarried maiden at eighteen years of age, leading up to full ordination at age twenty [Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken points out that Pācittiya 72 clarifies that attaining the age threshold does not exempt a candidate from the two-year probationary training period, functioning similarly for maidens to the way Pācittiya 66 functions for married women (*gihigatā*), while rendering the immediately preceding rule virtually redundant [Hüsken 1997]. Bhikkhu Sujato highlights the precision of the terminology, observing that the regulation specifically addresses maidens rather than adult women in general [Sujato 2009].

SuttaCentral records full parallels across all major extant Vinaya traditions, including the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese and Tibetan), Mahāsaṅghika, and Lokottaravāda (Sanskrit) vinayas [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus confirms substantial cross-linguistic alignment with the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* and the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus highlights extensive formulaic text reuse shared with adjacent ordination rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (notably Pācittiyas 63, 64, 66, 67, 73, and 75), several Khandhaka sections (Kd 1, 11, 13, 15, and 20), and later Vinaya treatises such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
